title: DFL11 12-round AES-192 MITM fault recovery

target.description: Full standardAES-192, 12 rounds. Fault injected betweenMC at rounds8 and9, not a reduced-round target. Recover both Kn and Kn-1 before master-key inversion; last subkey alone is insufficient.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.plaintext_model: Correct/faulty outputs paired for the same plaintext and key on each trial; plaintexts may vary.
assumptions: Section3.3 counts80unknownbits and80constraintbits; this is an expected-small-list heuristic, not a uniqueness theorem or numerical whole-attack success guarantee.

fault_model.target: Full AES state byte between the source two MixColumns operations.
fault_model.granularity: One random8-bit state byte per useful fault.
fault_model.value_control: Unknown nonzero byte error; not chosen value.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Correct/faulty outputs paired for the same plaintext and key on each trial; plaintexts may vary.

time.note: Section5.1:3*2^40 code operations plus2^40 Piret–Quisquater resolution, including both required subkeys.

data.note: Each useful fault has the correct counterpart; physical attempts not priced.

preprocessing.note: No numerical amount is reported for this resource.

success.description: No numerical whole-output success is supplied for this exact fault model and budget. Existing AppendixA ordered-vector dependency, literal-equation and headline/data qualifications are retained. The80-bit counting argument and the assertion of a unique intersection for ten pairs do not give a numerical finite-population probability. Known/fixed/random-location coefficients are tied to this exact model; location enumeration costs are not probabilities of acquiring useful faults. Section5.1 additionally solves Piret–Quisquater-type systems to recover Kn-1; no joint success for this longer-key completion is supplied.

review.scope: Exact18-page conference edition; targeted PDF3–4,7–14,17 and independent defining-passage review. Unique-intersection claims, expected survivors and long-key collect-until-complete statements do not quantify this endpoint at its stored budget. No probability was added; all components, literal-equation, ordered-vector, completion and resource obligations remain. Not a new full-paper audit.

This necessary relation does not certify the AppendixA tuple, collision uniqueness or a finite-budget recovery rate.
